key_insight: Molecular Prior Networks predict molecular affinity from labeled examples in a single transformer pass, matching state-of-the-art performance on the smallest support sets without task-specific training.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support early-stage drug discovery when measured affinity data are scarce, but clinical utility is not established.
method: Train a transformer across thousands of existing affinity datasets.
Predict query-molecule affinities using labeled support molecules in one forward pass.
Compare against kernel regression in a meta-learned feature space to probe the role of molecular similarity.
evidence_signal: On the regression variant of FS-Mol, the model matches state-of-the-art performance for the smallest support sets while being faster than existing methods.
watch_item: Generalization to new drug-discovery projects needs validation; the abstract does not report prospective experimental testing.
